items.title: Jane Jarvis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: Now I was friends with Mary Lou Williams, because she and Andy Kirk were at the Club Alabam... And that’s where I met her.

ctx.x: You started, you had some more formal education.

The big problem in music, is you had to either go to the education formula, or cast your wits against the world in jazz. Because there was no forum, mind you, eighty years ago. Not eighty years ago, well, in 1929 is when all this took place. In 1929, there was no place for a woman to play jazz. Now I was friends with Mary Lou Williams, because she and Andy Kirk were at the Club Alabam, which was right on my way to Bush Conservatory, and I used to sit and listen to the rehearsals. Big bands used to rehearse, you…
And Chicago was a pretty happening town for music, right?
